rubric_items.reason: All 14 known REQs are traced by a story (S-1 REQ-1..5, S-2 REQ-6..8, S-3 REQ-9..11 and REQ-14, S-4 REQ-12..13); no assumed REQs exist.
S-1 to S-3 each deliver one outcome; S-4 bundles two unrelated constraints (no medical history, everything else unchanged) into one story.

ACs are Given/When/Then and the local-midnight UTC case is good, but several would pass under likely wrong implementations: 365 days vs calendar months, any-old-Completed vs latest, UTC today, filter dropped under search/status, filter after paging.
20 per page, Asia/Kolkata, UTC+05:30 and the 12-month cutoff date are sourced or derived inline; other dates and counts are test fixtures.
Readable and consistent terms; a few Then clauses lean on 'as before the change' or a vague 'June 2026 date' instead of a concrete expected value.

findings.text: No S-2 AC tells 12 calendar months from 365 days, the option the user rejected in A-03: 25 Nov 2025 to 25 Nov 2026 is exactly 365 days, so a 365-day implementation passes every AC.

cites.quote: Given today is 25 November 2026 in Asia/Kolkata (12 calendar months earlier is 25 November 2025)
options: 12 calendar months, IST (proposed default) | 365 days

findings.suggested_fix: Add an AC whose window spans 29 Feb, e.g. today 1 March 2028 (12 calendar months earlier is 1 March 2027; 365 days earlier is 2 March 2027) and a last visit on 1 March 2027 local that must not be listed.

findings.text: The filter keys on the latest Completed visit, but no S-2 AC has a patient with an old Completed and a recent Completed appointment who must be excluded; an 'any Completed older than 12 months' query passes all ACs.

cites.quote: patient P3 has a COMPLETED appointment on 1 January 2025 and a later NO_SHOW appointment on 1 October 2026
only patients whose last visit was `more than 12 months ago`

findings.suggested_fix: Add an S-2 AC: patient with a COMPLETED appointment on 1 January 2025 and a later COMPLETED on 1 October 2026; with the filter on, the patient is not listed.

findings.text: S-2 ACs set 'today' as a date with no instant; computing today from the UTC clock only differs between 00:00 and 05:30 IST, so a UTC-today implementation passes unless the clock instant is pinned.

cites.quote: Given today is 25 November 2026 in Asia/Kolkata
is before the same calendar date 12 months before today

findings.suggested_fix: Pin now to an instant like 02:00 IST on 25 November 2026 (20:30 UTC on 24 November 2026) so a UTC-derived today (cutoff 24 Nov 2025) drops P1 and fails AC2.

findings.text: S-3 AC1 and AC2 seed only not-seen patients, so an implementation where search or the status filter replaces the not-seen filter still passes; nothing shows the filter also narrows the search/status result.

cites.quote: Given two patients not seen for a year, only one of whose name matches the search text
Given two patients not seen for a year, one of them Inactive
both narrow the same result

findings.suggested_fix: Add to each fixture a patient seen recently who also matches the search text (AC1) or is Inactive (AC2), and assert that patient is not listed.

findings.text: S-3 AC3 seeds only the 21 matching patients, so filtering after the page is fetched (in app code) passes; the AC cannot fail under that likely wrong implementation.

cites.quote: Given 21 patients not seen for a year, when staff turn the filter on, then page 1 lists 20 of them

findings.suggested_fix: Interleave recently seen patients by registration date (e.g. 21 not-seen among 30) and assert page 1 holds 20 not-seen patients and page 2 the 21st.

findings.text: REQ-13 keeps the rest of the list unchanged, but no S-4 AC covers the existing search and status filter with the new filter off, though they share the changed list query.

cites.quote: The rest of the patient list, and every other page, is `unchanged`.
newest registration first, with search and a status filter
then all patients are listed newest registration first at 20 per page, as before the change

findings.suggested_fix: Add S-4 ACs: with the not-seen filter off, search alone and the status filter alone return the same patients, including recently seen and never-visited ones, as before.

findings.text: S-4 AC2 and AC3 state the Then as 'as before the change' without naming the expected value, so the tester needs a baseline run to check them.

cites.quote: shows the same empty value as before the change

findings.suggested_fix: Name the current empty value and the current appointment format shown in the Next appointment column.

findings.text: S-1 AC4 gives months, not dates, so the expected Last visit date is not exact.

cites.quote: then the Last visit shows Dr B's name next to the June 2026 date

findings.suggested_fix: Use exact dates, e.g. 15 January 2026 and 10 June 2026, and assert 10 June 2026 with Dr B.
